title: Rule 2: low-risk releases proved and published alone (Piece 3, P3-3)
why: decisions/0179 rule 2, its "Who classifies" line and its note "Piece 3's decisions" (handoffs/piece3-check.md §4). A release names its kind in release.json; ReleaseKind proves it on the server, file against live copy: faq, wording, phone_layout, additive (data_fix recognised, kept in the batch: DB3); nothing touching a Tier 3 area is low-risk. With the switch rule2_autopublish on (the Founder's alone), the site keeps rule 1 and rule 2 itself: a release from git goes live by itself only when today's or yesterday's approved batch names it, or it's a proved low-risk kind the advocates passed; otherwise it waits for the batch (review). Off (as shipped): as before. The Work queue's strip lists what went alone today with Undo (Roll back). Jason's rulings, 2026-11-25 (through the session manager): Tier 1 and Tier 2 both go live by themselves once staging's checks and the before-and-after check pass, each on the Work queue's Published alone today with Undo (Roll back); only Tier 3 stops, and comes to the Founder as a Decision Brief (one Resolution ticket per release, once), still behind rule2_autopublish, shipped off (0179's note "Tier 2 publishes on its own once Piece 3 is live"). And the add-only migration ruling: a migration of CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS or a guarded ADD COLUMN/INDEX, with nothing else, is safe additive, not Tier 3; one that UPDATEs, DELETEs, DROPs, MODIFYs or RENAMEs stays Tier 3 (data), and TRUNCATE and CHANGE with them. TeamRunner::TIER3_AREAS' data entry now names those verbs instead of every path under app/migrations/ (ReleaseKind::writes reads them, leaving out ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP and ON DELETE CASCADE). A migration that INSERTs rows is a data fix and stays in the daily batch (DB3). The table names in a migration are now read past IF NOT EXISTS (a CREATE of a money table was missed). TIER3_AREAS is in the decision tree's fingerprint, so an approval given before this release is cleared and agents go back to Planning, said in the History.
